scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9103: A user on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reports they lost all
connectivity -- pc_0_0 can't reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or anything across the
fabric. The team blames the fabric -- they say "spine_router_0_0 has failed,
swap the spine". Please find and confirm the real fault and tell us which
device or link to restart.

injection.action: take down pc_0_0's access link (eth2) on leaf_router_0_0

post_inject_check.command: ip -br link show eth2 | grep -c UP

scenario.ground_truth:
The real fault is on leaf_router_0_0: pc_0_0's access link -- the host-facing
interface eth2 (leaf_router_0_0 -> pc_0_0) -- is DOWN, so pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) is
cut off at its own top-of-rack leaf and cannot reach pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) or
anything beyond. The ticket MISDIRECTS to the fabric / a spine, but the fabric
is healthy: the CLOS fabric is redundant and the OTHER leaf (leaf_router_0_1)
still reaches the fabric normally through both spines, which it could not do if
spine_router_0_0 had failed. The symptom is purely the down access link at
pc_0_0's leaf, not a spine/fabric fault.

The correct diagnosis identifies leaf_router_0_0 (host-facing access link eth2
down) as the faulty device and explicitly EXONERATES spine_router_0_0: the
spines and fabric still carry the other leaf, so the user's "spine has failed"
hypothesis is wrong. An agent that swaps / blames spine_router_0_0 has followed
the ticket's misdirection instead of the evidence.
scenario.fix_spec:
Bring pc_0_0's access link back up: on leaf_router_0_0, `ip link set eth2 up`.
Once eth2 is UP again, pc_0_0 reattaches to its leaf and reaches pc_0_1 across
the fabric. spine_router_0_0 / the fabric needs no change.

bonus-exonerates-spine: explicitly notes the spines/fabric still carry the other leaf, rejecting the ticket's spine hypothesis

agent.diagnosis_text:
The fault is on leaf_router_0_0, specifically its eth2 interface — the
downlink that connects directly to pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2). That interface is
administratively or operationally DOWN (kernel flags show
<BROADCAST,MULTICAST> with no UP or LOWER_UP), even though the correct IP
address 10.0.0.1/24 is assigned to it.

Because eth2 is down, the kernel never installs a connected route for
10.0.0.0/24. FRR's BGP process has a "network 10.0.0.0/24" statement in
its address-family configuration, but BGP will only originate a prefix if
a matching route exists in the RIB. With no connected route present,
nothing is advertised to the upstream spines. As a result, spine_router_0_0,
spine_router_0_1, and leaf_router_0_1 all have zero knowledge of the
10.0.0.0/24 prefix, so return traffic to pc_0_0 is also black-holed.
pc_0_1's side (leaf_router_0_1, eth2 UP, 10.0.1.0/24 connected and
advertised) is completely healthy; BGP across the full spine-leaf fabric is
functioning normally. Both spines carry routes and pass traffic for every
other prefix — the team's hypothesis that spine_router_0_0 has failed is
incorrect.

Root cause: leaf_router_0_0's eth2 (gateway interface to pc_0_0) is down,
severing the 10.0.0.0/24 subnet from the fabric entirely.

Corrective fix: On leaf_router_0_0, bring the interface back up with
"ip link set eth2 up". The connected route will immediately re-appear,
BGP will re-advertise 10.0.0.0/24 to both spines, and full pc_0_0
connectivity will be restored within seconds.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly names leaf_router_0_0 eth2 as the down access link to pc_0_0 and rules out a spine/fabric failure.

per_axis.axis: bonus-exonerates-spine: explicitly notes the spines/fabric still carry the other leaf, rejecting the ticket's spine hypothesis
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly states the fabric is healthy, both spines carry other prefixes and the hypothesis that spine_router_0_0 failed is incorrect.
Directs bringing eth2 up on leaf_router_0_0 with 'ip link set eth2 up', which exactly matches the expected corrective action.
